subject: research/house-adufees
professional: a municipal water/wastewater rate consultant who prepares capacity-charge (SDC) studies under AWWA M1, reviewing alongside a housing-policy economist who studies ADU development fees (Terner Center style). They would check first how the utility defines the charged area for a single-family tap (lot or floor area), whether an ADU that shares the main house's meter owes the ADU charge, whether the dollar figures match the adopted schedule, and whether the fee comparison is the one a homeowner actually faces (a house on a typical Denver lot, not a house 'charged on 2,000 sq ft').

Independent script `/usr/bin/python3.13 -I /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/5b35c5c9-389a-5954-9742-ad2b53d8c6ff/scratchpad/adu/indep.py` (imports nothing from the package; schedule constants typed from search-engine excerpts of Denver Water's 2026 SDC page and the Denver Gazette, not from data/sdc.csv): house on 2,000 sq ft Jul $5,400 / Jan $4,925, ADU saving 59.8%, step +5.60% ADU / +9.64% house, $4.52 vs $2.70 per sq ft, 6,000 sq ft $9,440/$8,365, slope over 22,000 $0.50, sewer totals $575/$9,225/$12,455, residual $12,005 and $5,525: all match results.txt. Provenance: denverwater.org, denvergov.org and marisstella.app are blocked by the session proxy (curl CONNECT 403; WebFetch ENOTFOUND), so no source page was read directly. Web-search excerpts of denverwater.org confirm base $3,380 + $1.01/sq ft (first 22,000) + $0.50 inside Denver from 1 July 2026, the January step $3,205 + $0.86, and ADU $2,055/$2,170 inside and $2,870/$3,030 outside: the SDC data are real, not invented. DOTI's $410 SAFE + $6,070 METRO, $425 and $150 could not be corroborated (search did not surface the PDF); not verified, not shown false. The defect: a Denver Water news item (search excerpt, denverwater.org/tap/fees-connect-denver-waters-system-increase) says a new single-family home 'on a 7,000 sq ft lot' goes to $10,450 after the phase-in, which is exactly 3,380 + 1.01 x 7,000. So the per-sq-ft rate is charged on lot area, and the headline '$5,400 for a house charged on 2,000 sq ft' and 'per floor sq ft the ADU is dearer ($4.52 vs $2.70)' answer a case no homeowner meets. On a Denver standard 50x125 ft lot (6,250 sq ft) a 2,000 sq ft house pays $9,692.50, $4.85 per floor sq ft, more than the ADU's $4.52; the per-sq-ft finding reverses for any lot over 5,606 sq ft, and the ADU saving is 77.6%, not 60%. Not 3: correct arithmetic on a wrong-reading input gives outputs a user would act on wrongly.

evidence.claims: Checked: '$2,170 ADU inside Denver from 1 July 2026, $2,055 before, $3,030 outside' (sdc.csv, corroborated by search excerpts) pass; 'house pays $3,380 + $1.01 per sq ft' pass; 'ADU pays 60% less than that house' arithmetic pass, but framed on a 2,000 sq ft charged area that the utility's own example shows is lot area, so the comparison a reader takes away (ADU 60% less than a house) understates it (77.6% on a 6,250 sq ft lot); 'Per floor sq ft the ADU is dearer ... $2.70 per sq ft if 2,000 is its floor area' fails: the 'if' is false per Denver Water's worked example, and on any lot over 5,606 sq ft the house is dearer per floor sq ft. 'The page does not say whether the per-sq-ft rate applies to lot or floor area' (README:16) and the Next step 'check the lot-or-floor reading against ... a worked example' (README:57): Denver Water published that worked example (7,000 sq ft lot -> $10,450), and the README even quotes the $10,450 figure from the Colorado Sun (README:38) yet treats it as a probe. '40-line model' (README:3) false (88). Sewer numbers: cited to DOTI PDFs, unreachable here; their framing as an 'upper-bound reading' is honest. Disclaimer 'Not advice, not a quote' present (README:16); AI assistance stated; MIT. The research index (research/README.md:710) repeats the 2,000 sq ft headline.
evidence.fitness: Could a researcher build on it? As a data point, partly: the Denver Water ADU and single-family SDC table is correctly transcribed and cited, and the sewer-fee split is a careful, hedged reading. As research, no: it is a fee-table lookup with subtraction, far below the PhD-level bar research/CLAUDE.md sets, with no question beyond one utility's tariff. Nearest prior work, none cited: Terner Center (UC Berkeley) 'It All Adds Up: The Cost of Housing Development Fees in Seven California Cities' (Mawhorter, Garcia and Raetz, 2018) and its ADU work (Chapple et al., 'Jumpstarting the Market for ADUs', 2017; later ADU fee/cost reports), which set the method for comparing fees per unit and per sq ft across unit types; California's 2019 ADU laws (AB 68, AB 881, SB 13; Gov. Code 65852.2(f), now 66324) that bar impact fees on ADUs under 750 sq ft and require proportional fees above, the obvious policy benchmark for 'should a 480 sq ft ADU pay a flat $2,170'; Colorado's own 2024 ADU law (HB24-1152) and its fee-reduction grant programme; local fee studies (HBA of Metro Denver development fee study, Common Sense Institute's cost-of-homebuilding report, which is the house-market $16,930 source) and AWWA M1 capacity-charge methodology (equivalent residential units by meter size or demand, which is why a flat ADU charge exists). Not new; sound in arithmetic but its central comparison uses the wrong charged area.
evidence.domain: Against standard SDC practice (AWWA M1: capacity charges scale with expected demand; Denver Water's single-family charge scales with lot area as a proxy for irrigation demand, as its 7,000 sq ft lot example shows): the schedule is transcribed right and the tier logic (first 22,000 sq ft, lower rate above) is right. Departures a rate consultant would flag first: (1) leaves lot-vs-floor open and headlines the floor reading, though the utility's own example settles it and irrigation-driven lot pricing is the known rationale; (2) compares the ADU to a house charged on 2,000 sq ft rather than to the marginal fee of adding an ADU to an existing lot, which is the homeowner's real choice; (3) does not settle whether an ADU on the house's existing meter owes the ADU charge (Denver Water says an ADU needs a water supply license and owes an additional SDC 'to run water service to the ADU', search excerpt), which drives the $2,745 'shared tap' total. The sewer side is handled with appropriate caution.

verdict: A small, honest tariff lookup with correct arithmetic and real data, whose headline comparison is framed on the wrong charged area. Every number reproduces (rerun byte-identical, 11 tests pass), and the Denver Water SDC and ADU figures match search excerpts of the utility's own page, so nothing is invented; the DOTI sewer fees could not be reached through the proxy. But Denver Water's own example prices a home on a 7,000 sq ft lot at $10,450, which is exactly the schedule on lot area, so the README's open 'lot or floor' question is already answered and its second headline ('per floor sq ft the ADU is dearer') reverses for any lot over 5,606 sq ft; the ADU saving on a standard 6,250 sq ft Denver lot is 77.6%, not 60%. Four of five seeded mutants survive, no prior work (Terner Center fee studies, California AB 68/SB 13, Colorado HB24-1152, AWWA M1) is cited, and as research it is a single-schedule lookup far below the PhD-level bar. Does not meet the bar.
